blueprint.intent_summary: Topic: choosing tiles for a home renovation. Audience: homeowners planning a renovation. Objective: help homeowners understand how different tile choices can affect the finished result and make a more informed selection. Business: generic tile retailer. Format: short-form social video.
blueprint.structural_approach: Open with a bold dual-contrast claim about tile choice outcomes, then hold the decision constant (same room type) while alternating between a mismatched tile choice and a well-matched one, reinforced by synchronized on-screen text, closing with a single visual break and pause before a guidance-seeking call to action.

mechanism_dispositions.application_rationale: Section 1 opens with a generalized claim contrasting two finished-result outcomes from tile choice, before any explanation, to prompt curiosity about which is which.
mechanism_dispositions.transferable_principle: Open with a bold, generalized dual-contrast claim before any explanation, prompting the audience to want resolution of the comparison.

mechanism_dispositions.application_rationale: Sections 2-5 hold the same room/use-case constant and alternate between the outcome of a poorly-suited tile choice and a well-suited one, preserving the same-subject-opposing-outcome relationship.
mechanism_dispositions.transferable_principle: Structure a narrative by alternating between two opposing behavioral outcomes tied to the same subject, reinforcing a before/after or type-A/type-B dichotomy.

mechanism_dispositions.application_rationale: Each demonstration and principle section pairs narration with on-screen text restating the same point, reinforcing the message visually without adding new content.
mechanism_dispositions.transferable_principle: Pair spoken narration with synchronized on-screen text restating the same content to reinforce the message through a parallel visual channel.

mechanism_dispositions.application_rationale: Visual continuity is kept through the comparison sections, then a single cut and a brief pause in sections 6-7 mark the shift into resolution and closing, signalling an ending.
mechanism_dispositions.transferable_principle: Maintain an unbroken visual continuity through most of a piece, then mark closure with a single cut and pauses to signal an ending.

constraints.copy_policy: Instructions only. This blueprint contains no final hook lines, captions, scripts, headlines, CTA wording or voiceover copy; those are produced downstream from these instructions.
constraints.performance_policy: Structural design logic is transferred; no performance, engagement, retention or conversion outcome is claimed or implied.

sections.section_purpose: Hook the audience with a broad claim that tile choice changes the finished look and feel of a room.
sections.content_instruction: State a generalized contrast between two different finished outcomes that can result from tile choice, without yet naming specific tiles or rooms, to create anticipation.
sections.visual_direction: Show a quick establishing shot of a renovation space, neutral and unbranded.
sections.text_direction: Short on-screen phrase mirroring the spoken contrast claim.
sections.speech_direction: Deliver the opening contrast claim in a confident, clear tone.
sections.pacing_direction: Single continuous shot, fast entry, no cuts.
prohibited_elements: guaranteed results
unsupported performance claims
copying the reference creator's relationship/gender narrative
source-specific names, wording, watermark or identity

sections.section_purpose: Show the mismatched tile outcome for a specific room/use case.
sections.content_instruction: Present one room/use case and demonstrate the negative consequence of an unsuitable tile choice for that context (e.g. durability, moisture, style mismatch), keeping the room constant for later contrast.
required_information: to be supplied: specific example room and tile type to illustrate mismatch
sections.visual_direction: Show the chosen room type with a tile finish that visibly clashes with its function.
sections.text_direction: On-screen caption naming the issue caused by the mismatch, synced to narration.
sections.speech_direction: Explain plainly why this tile choice underperforms in this context.
sections.transition_direction: Cut to matched version in next section.
prohibited_elements: guaranteed results
unsupported performance claims
copying the reference creator's relationship/gender narrative
source-specific names, wording, watermark or identity
limitations: Specific tile examples not supplied by intent

sections.section_purpose: Show the well-matched tile outcome for the same room/use case.
sections.content_instruction: Return to the same room/use case and show the positive outcome achieved with a well-suited tile choice, directly opposing section 2's outcome.
required_information: to be supplied: matching tile example for the same room
sections.visual_direction: Show the same room type with a tile finish appropriate to its function and aesthetic.
sections.text_direction: On-screen caption naming the benefit of the matched choice, synced to narration.
sections.speech_direction: Explain plainly why this tile choice works well in this context.
sections.transition_direction: Move into a second room example to broaden the point.
prohibited_elements: guaranteed results
unsupported performance claims
copying the reference creator's relationship/gender narrative
source-specific names, wording, watermark or identity

sections.section_purpose: Repeat the mismatch versus match contrast with a second, different room/use case to generalize the principle.
sections.content_instruction: Briefly show a second room/use case with the same mismatch-versus-match pairing, more quickly than sections 2-3, to reinforce that suitability depends on context rather than one universal best tile.
required_information: to be supplied: second example room and tile pairing
sections.visual_direction: Split or sequential shots contrasting the two outcomes in the new room type.
sections.text_direction: Short synced captions labeling each outcome.
sections.speech_direction: Summarize the same mismatch/match logic applied to the new context.
sections.pacing_direction: Slightly faster cadence than sections 2-3, still single continuous shots.
sections.transition_direction: Move to a summarizing principle statement.
prohibited_elements: guaranteed results
unsupported performance claims
copying the reference creator's relationship/gender narrative
source-specific names, wording, watermark or identity

sections.section_purpose: Derive a practical selection principle from the preceding comparisons.
sections.content_instruction: State the general rule that emerges from the contrasts: the right tile choice depends on the specific room and its use, not on any single tile being universally best.
sections.visual_direction: Neutral shot summarizing the space, perhaps a wider view of multiple tile samples.
sections.text_direction: On-screen summary line matching the spoken principle.
sections.speech_direction: Deliver the takeaway rule in a calm, instructive tone.
